moma:472.1941.title: The Starry Night
moma:472.1941.teaser: He painted it from a barred window in an asylum, the hills and the star are real, the village is not, and he thought it was a failure.

met:49.30.title: Cypresses
met:49.30.teaser: Painted the same summer, from the same asylum, and the tree he moved into The Starry Night stands here on its own.

aic:1942.51.title: Nighthawks
aic:1942.51.teaser: There is no door. Look for the way out of that diner and you will not find one, which is the whole painting.

met:57.92.title: Autumn Rhythm (Number 30)
met:57.92.teaser: He poured and flung the paint onto a canvas on the floor, the brush never touching it, and up close it is chaos. Step back and the whole wall begins to move.

met:JP1847.title: Under the Wave off Kanagawa (The Great Wave)
met:JP1847.where: The Japanese galleries, when it is on view
met:JP1847.teaser: The most famous wave in the world is a print the size of a placemat, and the small calm triangle it is about to swallow is Mount Fuji.

aic:1926.224.title: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte, 1884
aic:1926.224.teaser: Two years of tiny dots, no lines anywhere. Up close it is confetti, step back and a whole Sunday afternoon snaps into focus.

met:97.34.title: Washington Crossing the Delaware
met:97.34.teaser: Twelve feet tall and full of things that never happened, the flag not yet designed, the ice all wrong. It became the way a nation pictures its own founding anyway.

aic:1930.934.title: American Gothic
aic:1930.934.teaser: A farmer, a pitchfork, and a face the whole country has argued about since 1930. He meant it kindly. Nobody has ever been sure.

si-air:A19610048000.title: 1903 Wright Flyer
si-air:A19610048000.where: The Wright Brothers and the Invention of the Aerial Age, second floor
si-air:A19610048000.teaser: The pilot lay on his stomach and steered by sliding his hips, and everything this aircraft ever did, it did in one morning.

si-nmnh:G3551-00.title: Hope Diamond
si-nmnh:G3551-00.where: The Harry Winston Gallery, Janet Annenberg Hooker Hall of Geology, Gems and Minerals
si-nmnh:G3551-00.teaser: It is the size of a walnut, the blue is boron, and under ultraviolet light it glows red.

si-air:A19700102000.title: Apollo 11 Command Module Columbia
si-air:A19700102000.teaser: A three hundred and sixty three foot rocket left Florida and this twelve foot cone came back, and a laser scan in 2016 found the crew's handwriting still inside it.

si-nmah:star-spangled-banner.title: The Star-Spangled Banner
si-nmah:star-spangled-banner.artist: Mary Pickersgill, with Caroline Pickersgill, two nieces and Grace Wisher
si-nmah:star-spangled-banner.where: The Star-Spangled Banner chamber, second floor, off the central hall
si-nmah:star-spangled-banner.teaser: Count the stars and you get fourteen. The fifteenth was cut off and given away, and nobody today knows who has it.

nga:1967.6.1.a.title: Ginevra de' Benci
nga:1967.6.1.a.where: West Building, main floor, the Italian Renaissance rooms
nga:1967.6.1.a.teaser: The only Leonardo on public view in the Americas, and somebody sawed the bottom off it. Her hands are gone.

si-nmaahc:2009.50.39.title: Shawl Given to Harriet Tubman by Queen Victoria
si-nmaahc:2009.50.39.museum: National Museum of African American History and Culture
si-nmaahc:2009.50.39.where: Slavery and Freedom, the history galleries, Concourse level 3, when it is on view
si-nmaahc:2009.50.39.teaser: A queen invited her to the Jubilee, she did not go, and the lace came instead.

si-castle:smithson-crypt.title: The Crypt of James Smithson
si-castle:smithson-crypt.artist: Monument carved in Italy, unrecorded maker
si-castle:smithson-crypt.where: The small room immediately left of the north entrance, behind the iron gate
si-castle:smithson-crypt.teaser: He never once set foot in America, left it his whole fortune with no explanation, and the gate over his tomb is the fence from his grave in Genoa.

si-hmsg:picketts-charge.title: Pickett's Charge
si-hmsg:picketts-charge.where: Third floor, wrapping the inner ring
si-hmsg:picketts-charge.teaser: Eight canvases, nearly four hundred feet, wrapped around a round wall: an 1883 Gettysburg cyclorama buried under paper and then torn back open.

si-nmai:nnavm.title: National Native American Veterans Memorial, Warriors' Circle of Honor
si-nmai:nnavm.museum: National Museum of the American Indian
si-nmai:nnavm.where: Outdoors on the museum grounds, at the end of the curving stone path through the trees. Open at all hours, no ticket.
si-nmai:nnavm.teaser: Congress approved it in 1994 and nobody built it for twenty six years, and the cloths tied to the four lances were put there by visitors, who are invited to add one.
